This course begins there.

Nearly every organisation that has had a compliance failure had a policy covering it. The policy was not the problem.

Where compliance actually fails

It fails in the gap between the document and the decision. The policy was written for an auditor, so it is precise and unreadable, and the manager making a call on a Thursday evening does not consult it — they do what seems reasonable. The mandatory training was completed by everyone and changed nobody, because completion was the metric. Nobody owns the control, so when it fails there are three people who each assumed it was one of the others. And the code of conduct describes values rather than decisions, so it cannot be applied to the specific awkward situation in front of you.

What this course covers

Forty-one lessons from the environment down to the audit. The context first: legal systems and how business is regulated, labour legislation, international institutions and trade, what multinational structure changes about obligations, technology, and ethics and social responsibility as an operating matter rather than a poster. Then the risk and control framework: the heat map, the fraud triangle, cognitive bias and conflict of interest, ISO 31000, escalation, leadership-team dynamics, risk culture, the three lines of defence with the usual confusion in the second, the high-reliability organisation, and a code of conduct written so it can be applied. Then obligations across borders: multi-jurisdiction structures, mobility and assignments, unions, European works councils, the International Labour Organization and the OECD, global pay and tax equalisation, and — the core of it — employee data under GDPR and equivalent regimes, the compliance audit, and a plan for running an internal investigation. Then the most regulated area of workplace conduct: the legal requirements, prejudice and discrimination named plainly, and how to design mandatory training that changes behaviour and can be evidenced. Then documented procedures: what to document, BPMN, templates, implementation and a documentation project. Finally the audit itself: three audit levels starting with compliance, express scoring, a weighted checklist, four collection methods, gap analysis, RACI and a roadmap.

What this course does not cover

This is workplace and organisational compliance. It does not cover anti-money-laundering, sanctions screening, financial crime, third-party or supplier due diligence, or sector-specific regulatory reporting. It is also not legal advice and does not qualify you to give any — the obligations described vary by jurisdiction and change, and a lawyer remains a lawyer. If you came looking for financial-sector compliance, this is the wrong course and it is better that you know now.

You have already tried sleeping more, taking the weekend properly, and putting your phone in another room. It helped for about four days.

Why the usual advice does not work

Because none of it changes the arithmetic. Your workload did not arrive all at once — it accumulated, one reasonable request at a time, and nobody ever went back and renegotiated the total. You are still doing three things you took on temporarily two years ago. You have not handed anything over because the handover would take longer than the task. And underneath all of it there may be a question you have been avoiding, which is whether this is the right job at all. Recovery techniques treat the symptom of that. They are worth having. They are not a solution.

What this course covers

Thirty-five lessons. The mechanism first: what separates stress from burnout, where each comes from, how they are diagnosed, and how organisations measure them — useful because it explains why the environment you are in keeps producing the same result. Then workload: auditing where your hours actually go, SMART goals, the Eisenhower matrix, do-defer-delegate-delete, planning that survives a real week, Pomodoro, Getting Things Done, finding the time wasters, the psychology of procrastination, and recovery as part of the system rather than a reward. Then the lever that changes the total: why handing work over is hard, RACI, doing it so it does not come back, and buying your own hours back. Then your own pattern across five frameworks — MBTI, DISC, PAEI, Belbin and Hogan, the Big Five — which is mostly useful for telling "this person is impossible" apart from "this person is built differently". Then impostor syndrome and what you are actually worth. Finally the structural questions: whether the work matches your values, the career cube, a skills audit, financial pressure, and a genuine recovery strategy.

What this course is not

It is not a relaxation course. There is one lesson containing mindfulness and breathing material and that is all — if that is what you are looking for, this is the wrong purchase. It is also not clinical treatment. Burnout can shade into depression and anxiety, and those require a qualified professional; nothing here substitutes for that, and recognising when you have crossed that line is part of taking this seriously. What this course does is the structural work: workload, delegation, direction and money, which is where a great deal of workplace stress originates.

More than 1.6 million students have enrolled in my courses across 185 countries, and over 150,000 specialists have gone through my programmes. I hold PHRi and SHRM-CP certifications and represent HRCI in more than ten countries.

Selling to a business is not selling to a person in a different tone of voice. It is a different decision, made by a different number of people, over a different length of time.

Half the buying cycle happens without you in the room

Five to seven people sign off, each with a private reason to say no. The cycle runs for months. And for most of it the buyer is reading, comparing and asking colleagues — none of which appears anywhere in your analytics. By the time somebody fills in a form, the shortlist already exists and you are either on it or you are not. Three things follow, and this course is built on them. Until you can describe exactly who buys and what job they are hiring you to do, everything else is spray. Content here does not entertain — it arms the person who will have to defend this choice to their own manager. And marketing and sales cannot be measured separately, because the deal is produced by both.

What this course covers

Forty-three lessons. Who buys, first: being the voice of the customer inside your own company, product-market fit and how to sustain it, portfolio decisions with the BCG and McKinsey matrices, researching need through Jobs to be Done and design thinking, customer journey mapping, hypothesis validation, the north star metric and pirate metrics, monetisation models, unit economics with lifetime value against acquisition cost, scaling and risk. Finally one system instead of two departments: the revenue funnel through retention, where it leaks, acquisition cost against lifetime value, the system of record, forecasting deal quality, and a ninety-day rollout.

For business marketing that transfers with almost no loss, since a buyer and a candidate research you the same way before making contact. The larger disclosure is inside the sales block: nine of its sixteen lessons are about hiring, training and paying salespeople rather than about marketing. courseDetails.longDescription:
Wenn du viel mit Excel arbeitest, wirst du von den fantastischen Funktionen von Power Query absolut begeistert sein.

Power Query ist seit einigen Jahren in Excel fest integriert - und es ist eine der am meisten unterschätzten Funktionen in Excel!

Du kannst eine Power Query Abfrage beispielsweise dazu verwenden, um die Werte aus Dutzenden Tabellen in Sekundenschnelle zusammenzufassen und die gesamten Dateien danach in einer einzigen Pivot-Tabelle zu verarbeiten.

In der Unternehmensanalyse muss in der Lage sein, mit verschiedenen Datenquellen und Strukturen zu arbeiten, und hier kommen die Optionen Gruppieren, Pivotieren und Entpivotieren von Power Query ins Spiel. So kannst du selbst schlecht angelieferte Daten vollautomatisch in ein angenehmes Format bringen, das von Menschen (und Pivot-Tabllen) leicht zu lesen ist.

Erinnerst du dich noch daran, wie du das erste Mal ein Auto gefahren bist?

Die Arbeit mit Power Query ist so einfach, dass du damit Excel quasi auf "Tempomat" stellst.

Power Query ist der kleine Motor, der deine Arbeit mit Excel ab sofort antreibt. Mit Power Query kannst du Daten von überall her herunterladen, sie in eine Art Datenbank umwandeln und dann mit allen Funktionen von Excel analysieren.

Jetzt ist Schluss mit Copy/Paste-Orgien und Zusatz-Spalten!

Pivot-Tabellen sind ein unglaublich wichtiges Werkzeug für die Analyse von Daten, aber es kostet viel Zeit, sie richtig einzurichten, weil man die Daten in der richtigen Form benötigt. Mit Power Query kannst du deine Daten auf eine kreative Weise automatisieren und schnell und einfach lesbar machen.

Das Erlernen von Power Query wird deine Produktivität erheblich steigern und es dir ermöglichen, Daten-Tabellen in weniger als der 20% der Zeit zu erstellen, als dies bei der manuellen Erstellung der Fall wäre. Egal, ob es sich um ein paar Tage oder nur mehrere Stunden Arbeit handelt, Power Query spart dir jeden Tag eine Menge Zeit und Geld!

Inhalt:

  • Intro und Motivation zu Power Query

  • Extrahieren von Text-Teilen

  • Alle Dateien eines Ordners zusammenfassen

  • Zur Erinnerung - Unterschied Tabellenblatt, Liste und definierte Tabelle

  • Daten aus dem Internet abrufen mit Power Query, zum Beispiel Aktienkurse

  • Der Grund für verschiedene Formate von Daten

  • Fremdes Gebietsschema (z.B. Dezimalzahlen mit Punkt statt Komma) umwandeln

  • Fremdes Datumsformat in unser Format konvertieren

  • Manuelles Zerlegen von problematischen Werten (z.B. aus SAP Download)

  • Weitere extrem nützliche Datum-Funktionen

  • Motivation + Unterschied Transformieren und Spalte hinzufügen am Beispiel Runden

  • Bedingte Spalte mit WENN-Formel kinderleicht einfügen

  • Berechnungen über Spalten, mit Spalten, zwischen Spalten in Excel mit Power Query

  • Eine Pivot-Tabelle mit Daten aus Power Query

  • Die einfachste Aggregierung ANZAHL

  • Aufsummieren wie bei einer Pivot Tabelle direkt beim Import

  • Mehrere Spalten in die berechnete Tabelle aufnehmen

  • Weitere Merkmale in die Pivot-Tabelle einfügen

  • Daten bei Bedarf transponieren (Zeilen und Spalten tauschen)

  • So entstehen pivotierte Daten

  • Daten aus einer Pivot-Tabelle rekonstruieren (entpivotieren)

Mit Power Query kannst du nicht nur Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen importieren, sondern auch effektiv und zeitsparend aufbereiten. Dies erleichtert die Erstellung von Berichten, Dashboards und anderen Visualisierungen, die für die Entscheidungsfindung in deinem Unternehmen oder Projekt unerlässlich sind. Durch die Automatisierung von Routineaufgaben kannst du dich auf die wichtigen Aspekte deiner Arbeit konzentrieren und gleichzeitig die Qualität und Genauigkeit deiner Ergebnisse sicherstellen.

Die Integration von Power Query in Excel ermöglicht es dir, Daten aus einer Vielzahl von Quellen, wie z.B. Webseiten, SQL-Datenbanken oder SharePoint-Listen, abzurufen und zu verbinden. Mit der Fähigkeit, Verbindungen zu externen Datenquellen einfach herzustellen, kannst du den Umfang deiner Analysen erweitern und aktuellere und aussagekräftigere Informationen erhalten.

Die Verwendung von Power Query in Kombination mit Pivot-Tabellen ermöglicht es dir, komplexe Zusammenhänge in deinen Daten zu erkennen und die wichtigsten Erkenntnisse herauszufiltern. Anstatt stundenlang mit manuellen Berechnungen und Tabellenkalkulationen zu kämpfen, kannst du deine Zeit nutzen, um aussagekräftige Visualisierungen zu erstellen und deine Ergebnisse mit Kollegen und Vorgesetzten zu teilen.

The role of a Chief Product Officer emerges precisely when a product stops being a collection of initiatives and becomes a strategic business asset. A CPO is not responsible for backlogs and roadmaps, but for a portfolio of decisions, investments in growth, team focus, and long-term value for both the customer and the company.


The path to this role is rarely obvious. Experience in product management, metrics, and team leadership is necessary, but not sufficient. At the CPO level, a different mindset is required: systemic, portfolio-driven, business-outcome-oriented, and focused on scale. Mistakes here are costly—wrong priorities, lost time, missed markets.


This course is designed as a practical roadmap for transitioning into the CPO role. It shows how product decisions are made at the C-level and why they define a company’s growth trajectory. The focus is on real executive challenges faced by product leaders, not abstract models “in a vacuum”.


Course program:

— the role and mission of the CPO, the evolution from product management to product leadership;

— building product strategy and linking it to business goals;

— product portfolio management and investment decisions;

— working with the market, customers, and validation of product hypotheses;

¿PORQUÉ ES IMPORTANTE OPTIMIZAR LAS IMÁGENES DE UN SITIO WEB?

Optimizar las imágenes de un sitio web es crucial porque reduce el peso de los archivos sin perder calidad visual. Esto acelera la carga de la página, mejora el posicionamiento SEO en Google, optimiza la experiencia del usuario (lo que aumenta las conversiones y ventas) y ahorra espacio en el servidor.

El proceso de optimización se divide en tres pilares principales:

Tamaño y dimensiones: Ajustar la imagen a las medidas exactas (en píxeles) en las que se va a mostrar, evitando subir imágenes inmensas que la web solo reducirá visualmente.

Compresión: Reducir el peso en kilobytes (KB o MB) utilizando herramientas de compresión para que el navegador del usuario descargue la imagen mucho más rápido.

Formatos adecuados: Usar formatos modernos como WebP para fotografías, o PNG/SVG para logotipos e íconos con fondos transparentes.

Las imágenes sin optimizar son la causa principal de los sitios web lentos. Esto genera tasas de rebote más altas (usuarios que abandonan la página antes de que cargue) y penalizaciones por parte de los motores de búsqueda.

  • Compresión avanzada: Ofrece tres modos: Lossy (máxima reducción con pérdida de calidad casi imperceptible), Glossy (alta calidad visual) y Lossless (sin pérdida de calidad).
